statuses.title: docs: prepare public source-repository messaging
statuses.note: Repository IS public (GitHub API: "private": false, "visibility": "public", stars 2, forks 0). Public-facing messaging is largely in place: README.md:12-16 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:3-7 both carry the identical "Work in progress ... do not rely on it for production or compliance-sensitive privacy guarantees" disclaimer; repo description, homepage (https://jetbrains-research.github.io/opaque/, HTTP 200) and six topics are set; only two email addresses exist anywhere in tracked files (security@jetbrains.com in SECURITY.md:12, codeofconduct@jetbrains.com in CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md:8) - no employee handles, no internal mail. Caveats filed as findings: the README/installation "Extras" blocks omit the registry index and resolve to an unrelated PyPI project (finding 3); internal infrastructure identifiers survive in .teamcity/pom.xml:18 and .github/workflows/build-devcontainer.yaml:77 (finding 2); an orphan 60 KB internal research diary sits at the public repo root (finding 11).

statuses.title: docs: add a public vulnerability reporting policy
statuses.note: SECURITY.md exists at the repository root - the primary location GitHub scans (root, docs/, .github/) - added by 44a494c2 "docs: add vulnerability reporting policy (#560)" and unchanged in the 4b13d82..12146ec4 delta. It names a real private contact (security@jetbrains.com, SECURITY.md:12), links the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy (https://www.jetbrains.com/legal/docs/terms/coordinated-disclosure/ - verified HTTP 200) and the PGP key page (https://www.jetbrains.com/privacy-security/ - HTTP 200), states supported versions, required report contents, and an explicit "what is not a security report" split that routes ordinary DP-mechanism defects to the public tracker. Caveats: (a) no concrete disclosure window is stated - SECURITY.md:41-42 only says "allow reasonable time for a fix or mitigation" and delegates timing to the JetBrains policy; (b) GitHub's own private reporting channel is OFF (GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/private-vulnerability-reporting -> {"enabled": false}), so the "Report a vulnerability" button is absent and the email address is the only private route. Filed as finding 9.

statuses.title: docs: add a code of conduct for public contributions
statuses.note: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md exists at the repository root (added by b5887f40 "docs: add JetBrains code of conduct (#561)", untouched in the delta). statuses.title: ci: harden repository controls before public visibility
statuses.note: Substantially in force and verified live via the API. Ruleset id 12831618 "main" is enforcement=active on ~DEFAULT_BRANCH with: deletion protection, non_fast_forward, required_linear_history, pull_request (required_approving_review_count 1, required_review_thread_resolution true, allowed_merge_methods [squash]), copilot_code_review, and 7 required status checks (Build documentation, Format Python, Format Rust, Conventional Commits PR title, Python tests, Rust tests, Qodana / Qodana). Workflow-side hardening is real: every third-party action is SHA-pinned with a version comment; no pull_request_target anywhere; .github/workflows/junie.yml:17-66 gates every comment/issue trigger on author_association in [OWNER, MEMBER, COLLABORATOR] and interpolates only literal constants into action inputs; junie-review.yml:19 and the three CUDA lanes in pr.yml:137-186 gate on head.repo.full_name == github.repository so fork PRs never reach the self-hosted GPU runner or a secret-bearing job; publish jobs use environment: release with contents: read. Caveats: (a) secret scanning / push protection / code scanning state is NOT verifiable from here - GET .../secret-scanning/alerts and .../vulnerability-alerts are blocked by the agent proxy (403 "not permitted through this proxy"), and repos.security_and_analysis came back null for this token, so that half of the issue is cannot-verify; (b) private vulnerability reporting is off (finding 9); (c) bypass_actors contains RepositoryRole actor_id 5 with bypass_mode "always" (repository admins bypass the whole ruleset); (d) the "Qodana / Qodana" required check can never report for a fork PR (finding 7).

statuses.title: build: migrate package publishing to a JetBrains-managed registry
statuses.note: Both publish paths target the JetBrains-managed registry and reference credentials by name only. .github/workflows/ci.yml:200-241 (publish-dev-wheels, environment: release, permissions contents: read, gated on all 11 test jobs) and .github/workflows/release.yml:122-133 (publish, environment-gated, after a manifest reverify) both set TWINE_USERNAME: ${{ vars.JETBRAINS_PACKAGES_USERNAME }} and TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.JETBRAINS_PACKAGES_TOKEN }} and upload to https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/legacy/ via .github/scripts/twine_upload.py. The unregistered-name exposure this publishing choice creates is a separate finding (1).

statuses.title: Modularize and reuse more in CI/CD
statuses.note: Modularization is real and did NOT drop lane coverage. Five reusable workflows (python-tests.yml, rust-tests.yml, qodana.yml, build-distributions.yml, validate-distributions.yml) plus four composite actions (setup-python, setup-rust, run-qodana, upload-python-coverage) are called from pr.yml and ci.yml. I compared every lane's marker expression against AGENTS.md's documented list and all 13 match exactly - PR linux-amd64 "not cuda and not mps and not slow and not distributed" (pr.yml:73), PR distributed "distributed and not cuda" (pr.yml:84), PR macOS "not cuda and not slow and not distributed" (pr.yml:114), main linux-amd64 drops "and not slow" (ci.yml:30), main CUDA locked is bare "cuda" (ci.yml:98), CUDA dependency-boundary lanes stay "cuda and not slow" (ci.yml:111,124). The authors deliberately added matrix-independent gate jobs "Python tests" (pr.yml:184-217) and "Rust tests" (pr.yml:221-235) for branch protection, and the Python gate's jq explicitly tolerates skipped python-tests-cuda* legs. Caveat: that same pattern was not applied to Qodana - "Qodana / Qodana" is required directly and its caller job is fork-guarded, so it cannot report on fork PRs (finding 7).

findings.title: Dependency-confusion defensive registration on PyPI covers only 4 of the 10 published distribution names; the other 6 are free for anyone to claim
findings.line: 34-45 (package table) and 66-81 (install commands); names defined in pyproject.toml:83-94 workspace.members
findings.claim: Opaque publishes to a private-namespace index (packages.jetbrains.team) rather than PyPI, which is the classic dependency-confusion setup. The team recognised this and on 2026-08-12 published JetBrains security-tooling defensive stubs on PyPI at version 999.9.9 whose description reads verbatim "This public copy of the package is a stub published on pypi.org designed to mitigate risks from Dependency Confusion" - but only for opaque-accounting, opaque-auditing, opaque-dpftrl and opaque-optimizers. Querying pypi.org/pypi/<name>/json for every distribution the repo builds shows opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers and opaque-alignment all return 404, i.e. unregistered and claimable by any third party today. The umbrella name is worse: `opaque` on PyPI is already an unrelated third-party project (opaque 1.0.0, "python libopaque wrapper", author Stefan Marsiske), so it cannot be defensively held at all. The repository's public README table and import-layout block (README.md:34-45, 48-61) publish the exact unregistered names.
findings.failure_scenario: An attacker registers `opaque-engine` and `opaque-base` on PyPI (both currently 404) with malicious sdists. Any of these then executes attacker code: (a) a user who reads README.md's package table and types `pip install opaque-engine` without the JetBrains index - the documented per-package install surface in AGENTS.md's installation matrix uses exactly these bare names; (b) any environment that adds PyPI as an extra index (`pip install --extra-index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/... opaque`) - pip merges candidates across indexes and picks the highest version, so a 999.9.9-style attacker release wins; (c) any uv configuration with index-strategy = "unsafe-best-match". Because opaque-base and opaque-engine are transitive dependencies of every other wheel, a single captured name reaches every Opaque install in that environment, inside a DP training pipeline that handles sensitive data.
evidence: pypi.org/pypi/opaque-accounting/json -> version 999.9.9, single file opaque_accounting-999.9.9.tar.gz uploaded 2026-08-12T15:05:40, description: 'This public copy of the package is a stub published on pypi.org designed to mitigate risks from Dependency Confusion. ... contact us: security-tooling@jetbrains.com'; identical stubs for opaque-auditing (15:05:27), opaque-optimizers (15:05:34), opaque-dpftrl (15:05:46)
pypi.org/pypi/{opaque-base,opaque-engine,opaque-dpsgd,opaque-patches,opaque-transformers,opaque-alignment}/json -> HTTP 404 for all six
pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json -> {'name': 'opaque', 'version': '1.0.0', 'summary': 'python libopaque wrapper', 'author': 'Stefan Marsiske'} - an unrelated third-party project
pyproject.toml:83-94 workspace.members lists all ten package directories; README.md:34-45 publishes the ten distribution names in a table
.github/workflows/ci.yml:236-241 and release.yml:124-133 publish these names to https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/legacy/, never to PyPI
findings.fix_sketch: Ask JetBrains security-tooling (security-tooling@jetbrains.com, the address in the existing stubs) to publish the same 999.9.9 defensive stub for opaque-base, opaque-engine, opaque-dpsgd, opaque-patches, opaque-transformers and opaque-alignment, and to re-run that registration whenever a new opaque-* distribution is added (add it as a checklist item next to the workspace.members list). For the umbrella name, which is taken, state explicitly in README.md and docs/getting-started/installation.md that `opaque` on PyPI is a different project and that the index flag is mandatory, and never document a bare `pip install opaque*` without --index-url.

findings.title: Internal JetBrains infrastructure identifiers are committed in the public repository: an access-controlled TeamCity server hostname and an internal GCP Artifact Registry project
findings.claim: Marble #578 ("Remove JetBrains-internal specifics from documentation") is closed, but two internal infrastructure identifiers remain in tracked configuration at origin/main, which is public. `.teamcity/pom.xml:18` hardcodes `<teamcity.server.url>https://jbr-fed.teamcity.com</teamcity.server.url>`; that host is access-controlled (anonymous GET returns HTTP 401), so this discloses the name of a non-public CI server plus, via `.teamcity/README.md` and `.teamcity/settings.kts`, its intended project layout, agent pool (`Linux-Large`, `teamcity.agent.jbHosted`) and pipeline id (`Opaque_LinuxAmd64Tests`). `.github/workflows/build-devcontainer.yaml:77` hardcodes `GAR_IMAGE: europe-west4-docker.pkg.dev/gke-dev-dws-jbr/ml/opaque-devcontainer`, disclosing an internal Google Cloud project id (`gke-dev-dws-jbr`) and repository (`ml`) that the GitHub Actions OIDC workload identity pushes images into. Neither is a secret in the credential sense, but both are precisely the kind of internal specific #578 and #553 claimed to have removed, and neither serves any public reader.
findings.failure_scenario: A public reader of the repository learns the hostname of an internal JetBrains TeamCity instance and the project/repository coordinates of an internal GCP Artifact Registry. That is reconnaissance input for credential-stuffing or phishing against the TeamCity instance and for probing/targeting the GAR path, and it widens the blast radius of any future leak of GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER / GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL because the attacker already knows where to push. The `.teamcity` prototype is additionally dead weight: nothing in .github/workflows references TeamCity, AGENTS.md documents GitHub Actions as the CI, and .teamcity/README.md forward-references a migration ("replaces the GitHub Actions Linux amd64 test matrix") that has not happened - itself a violation of AGENTS.md's "forward-references to features that don't yet exist don't belong anywhere".

GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque -> "private": false, "visibility": "public"

findings.fix_sketch: Replace the literal TeamCity server URL in .teamcity/pom.xml with a Maven property supplied at generate time (`-Dteamcity.server.url=...`) or delete the `.teamcity` prototype entirely until the migration is real, and drop its forward-referencing README. In .github/workflows/build-devcontainer.yaml move the GAR image path to a repository variable (`${{ vars.GAR_IMAGE }}`) alongside the two GCP vars it already uses by name, so no internal project id is committed. Re-run a grep for internal host/project identifiers over ALL tracked files, not only docs prose, before declaring #578 complete.

findings.title: Public install documentation's "Extras" commands omit the registry index and resolve to an unrelated PyPI project named `opaque`
findings.claim: README.md:67-72 and docs/getting-started/installation.md:19-27 correctly teach `pip install opaque --index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/`. The Extras blocks immediately below them then drop the flag entirely: README.md:78-81 and installation.md:33-36 show four bare commands (`pip install "opaque[auditing]"`, `"opaque[dpftrl]"`, `"opaque[transformers]"`, `"opaque[all]"`). `--index-url` does not persist across shell invocations, so a reader who copies these lines resolves `opaque` from PyPI, where `opaque` is a different project - version 1.0.0, "python libopaque wrapper" by Stefan Marsiske, which has none of these extras.
findings.failure_scenario: A new user follows the README top to bottom: the first command installs the real Opaque from the JetBrains index; the next line, `pip install "opaque[all]"`, silently downloads the unrelated libopaque wrapper from PyPI, warns only `WARNING: opaque 1.0.0 does not provide the extra 'all'`, and overwrites the installed `opaque` distribution. The user's `import opaque.dpsgd` then fails, or - worse in a CI image built from the docs - the wrong `opaque` ends up in the environment used to reason about differential privacy. The same hazard applies to `uv add` since the second block never re-specifies `--index`.
evidence: README.md:78-81 — `pip install "opaque[auditing]"` / `"opaque[dpftrl]"` / `"opaque[transformers]"` / `"opaque[all]"`, no index flag
docs/getting-started/installation.md:33-36 — identical four commands, no index flag, directly under the `--index-url` block at :19-27
pypi.org/pypi/opaque/json -> {'version': '1.0.0', 'summary': 'python libopaque wrapper', 'author': 'Stefan Marsiske'}
https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/opaque/ lists opaque-0.15.0-py3-none-any.whl etc. — the real project is only on that index
findings.fix_sketch: Repeat `--index-url https://packages.jetbrains.team/pypi/p/fed/python/simple/` on every install command in README.md and docs/getting-started/installation.md, or restructure the pages to configure the index once persistently (a `pip config set global.index-url ...` / `[[tool.uv.index]]` snippet) and say so explicitly. Add a one-line warning that the `opaque` name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project. Under ARC-011 these blocks are the tagged executable installation scenarios, so the post-build validator should run them verbatim in a clean environment - which would have caught this.

findings.title: The committed uv.lock still resolves accelerate 1.14.0, which carries an open GitHub-reviewed advisory with a released fix
findings.claim: Marble #574 ("remediate dependency security alerts before public visibility") is closed, but the lockfile at origin/main pins a version with a live advisory. Querying every one of the 218 PyPI packages in uv.lock against OSV.dev returns exactly one hit: accelerate 1.14.0, affected by GHSA-4j2p-28q2-5m79 / CVE-2026-69112 / PYSEC-2026-3804 - path traversal and denial of service via unsanitised `weight_map` entries in sharded-checkpoint indexes consumed by `load_checkpoint_in_model` and `load_checkpoint_and_dispatch` (CWE-22, CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H, MODERATE, github_reviewed 2026-09-08). The advisory's range is `last_affected: 1.14.0` and accelerate 1.15.0 is already published on PyPI, so a fix exists and was simply not taken. accelerate reaches the lock transitively through peft 0.20.0 and trl 1.12.0, i.e. through opaque-transformers / opaque-alignment / opaque-patches[transformers].
findings.failure_scenario: Anyone reproducing the project with the documented `uv sync --group dev --all-packages --extra all` - every contributor and every CI lane - gets accelerate 1.14.0. A DP fine-tuning run that loads a sharded checkpoint from an untrusted or partially-trusted source (an arbitrary Hugging Face Hub repo, which is exactly what examples/train_*.py do) can be made to read arbitrary files off the runner via `../` entries in the shard index, or to hang forever on a named pipe. On the self-hosted persistent GPU runner (`GPU-runner-001`) an arbitrary-file-read primitive is materially worse than on an ephemeral one.

uv.lock:2862 and :4146 — accelerate is required by peft 0.20.0 and trl 1.12.0

findings.title: third_party_provenance.toml misattributes riskcal to a nonexistent google-research repository, and one upstream's homepage is prose rather than a URL
findings.claim: ARC-009 requires that "repository provenance references resolve to real attributed sources". Two entries fail. (1) The riskcal upstream declares `homepage = "https://github.com/google-research/riskcal"`; no such repository exists - a GitHub search for `riskcal in:name` returns the real project at `interpretable-dp/riskcal` ("Measure and calibrate operational privacy risks for differentially private algorithms"), and PyPI's riskcal metadata gives project_urls.Repository = https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal.git with authors Bogdan Kulynych and Juan Felipe Gomez. The manifest therefore credits Google Research for work by other authors. (2) The "Random-allocation reference implementation" entry puts a sentence in the `homepage` field - `homepage = 'ICML 2026 reference implementation for "Efficient privacy loss accounting for subsampling and random allocation"'` - which is not a resolvable reference at all, for code the manifest marks `disposition = "adapted"`, `requires_notice = true` and whose derived files ship in opaque-dpsgd.
findings.failure_scenario: A downstream consumer performing an OSS license/attribution review of the published opaque-dpsgd and opaque-accounting wheels follows third_party_provenance.toml - the document ARC-009 designates as the machine-readable provenance source of truth that will generate or validate NOTICE - and cannot locate the riskcal upstream (404) to confirm its MIT terms, and cannot locate the random-allocation upstream at all to confirm its Apache-2.0 terms or satisfy the notice obligation the manifest itself asserts. On a public repository this is a live misstatement of the project's attribution posture, and it will propagate straight into NOTICE the moment the planned generator is built on top of this file.

findings.fix_sketch: Change the riskcal homepage to https://github.com/interpretable-dp/riskcal. Give the random-allocation entry a resolvable `homepage` (the arXiv/proceedings URL or the reference implementation's repository) and, if only a paper exists, add a separate `citation` field rather than overloading `homepage`. Add a tiny validator to CI that parses third_party_provenance.toml and asserts every `files` path exists and every `homepage` is an absolute http(s) URL - the same script used here found both defects in one pass, and it is behavioural rather than an inventory check so it does not conflict with #586's intent.

findings.title: The repository's squash setting discards every PR body, contradicting AGENTS.md and the PR template and disabling git-cliff's BREAKING CHANGE detection
findings.line: 97-118 (Pull requests section); config verified via the repository API
findings.claim: AGENTS.md states "The PR title becomes the commit subject; the PR body becomes the commit body (repo-level squash setting = `PR_TITLE` + `PR_BODY`). Both feed `git-cliff`", and .github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 repeats "On squash merge the body becomes the commit body that git-cliff reads." The repository is actually configured with `squash_merge_commit_title: "PR_TITLE"` but `squash_merge_commit_message: "BLANK"`. Every one of the 124 delta commits confirms it: their bodies are empty apart from GitHub-generated `Co-authored-by:` trailers. This is not only stale documentation - cliff.toml:36 contains `{ body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE", group = "Breaking" }` and sets `protect_breaking_commits = true`, both of which read the commit BODY, and AGENTS.md:110-111 explicitly tells contributors that a breaking change may be declared with "a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the body".
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor follows AGENTS.md and declares a breaking change with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the PR body instead of a `!` in the title (both are documented as equivalent). The squash merge drops the footer, so the commit body is empty; git-cliff's body parser never fires, the commit is categorised by its type prefix (e.g. `refactor` -> "Changed") instead of "Breaking", and the drafted GitHub Release for that version ships with no Breaking section. Downstream users upgrading on those notes hit an undeclared breaking change. Separately, every release's "What's changed" and permanent `git log` lose the 2-4 sentences of rationale the PR template asks for - exactly the 'why' AGENTS.md says to preserve for "a future spelunker".
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque -> {"squash_merge_commit_title": "PR_TITLE", "squash_merge_commit_message": "BLANK", "allow_merge_commit": false, "allow_rebase_merge": false}
AGENTS.md 'Pull requests': 'The PR title becomes the commit subject; the PR body becomes the commit body (repo-level squash setting = `PR_TITLE` + `PR_BODY`)'
.github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 'On squash merge the body becomes the commit body that git-cliff reads.'
git log 4b13d82..12146ec4 --pretty='%b' — every commit body is empty or contains only Co-authored-by trailers (e.g. 873de427, 026200fd, e44d6ab6, 79acf31d, 0a002a50 have entirely empty bodies)
cliff.toml:36 { body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE", group = "Breaking" }; cliff.toml:40 protect_breaking_commits = true
AGENTS.md 'Breaking change: append `!` (`feat(dpsgd)!: …`) or include a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer in the body.'
findings.fix_sketch: Pick one and make config and docs agree. Either set the repository's squash commit message to PR_BODY (matching what AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the PR template already promise and what cliff.toml's body parser needs), or - if empty bodies are deliberate - remove the `body = ".*BREAKING CHANGE"` parser from cliff.toml, drop the 'BREAKING CHANGE footer' option from AGENTS.md so `!` in the title is the only supported declaration, and rewrite .github/pull_request_template.md:7-9 accordingly. Setting PR_BODY is the smaller change and preserves the documented behaviour.

findings.title: The required status check "Qodana / Qodana" can never report on a fork pull request, so the documented external-contribution path cannot merge
findings.claim: The active main ruleset requires seven status checks, one of which is the context "Qodana / Qodana" produced by pr.yml's `qodana` job calling the reusable qodana.yml `scan` job (both named "Qodana"). That caller job is guarded by `github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, so for a pull request opened from a fork the job is skipped, the reusable workflow is never instantiated, and the "Qodana / Qodana" check context is never created - a required check that never reports blocks merge. The authors clearly understood this hazard elsewhere: pr.yml:184-217 and :221-235 add matrix-independent gate jobs named "Python tests" and "Rust tests" with `if: always()` whose jq explicitly treats skipped `python-tests-cuda*` legs as success, with the comment "Keep a stable, matrix-independent check name for branch protection rules". No equivalent gate exists for Qodana. Meanwhile docs/development/index.md:3,10-11 documents the fork workflow and README.md:186 points contributors at it.
findings.failure_scenario: An external contributor forks the repository as docs/development/index.md instructs, opens a PR, and every check goes green except "Qodana / Qodana", which sits permanently as 'Expected - waiting for status to be reported'. The PR cannot be merged by anyone other than a repository admin using the ruleset's bypass. For a project that went public specifically to accept outside contributions (Marble #553/#557), the advertised contribution path is unmergeable by design. The same guard also means the fork PR receives no static-analysis coverage at all, which is the case where untrusted code most needs it.
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/rulesets/12831618 -> required_status_checks includes {"context": "Qodana / Qodana"}; the pull_request rule requires 1 approving review; bypass_actors = [{actor_type: RepositoryRole, actor_id: 5, bypass_mode: always}]
.github/workflows/pr.yml:252-257 — qodana job `if: (success() || failure()) && !github.event.pull_request.draft && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository`, `name: Qodana`
.github/workflows/qodana.yml:29-31 — jobs.scan has `name: Qodana`, so the composed check context is 'Qodana / Qodana'

.github/workflows/pr.yml:182-186 — comment 'Keep a stable, matrix-independent check name for branch protection rules' above the `python-tests` gate job, and pr.yml:195-217 jq that tolerates skipped CUDA legs — the pattern deliberately applied to Python/Rust but not Qodana
docs/development/index.md:3,10-11 'This guide is for contributors working from a GitHub fork ... Fork JetBrains-Research/opaque, then clone your fork'; README.md:186 links it
Repository is public with allow_forking: true (GitHub API)
findings.fix_sketch: Add a stable gate job to pr.yml in the same shape as `python-tests` / `rust-test-gate` - e.g. a job named "Qodana" with `if: always()` and `needs: [qodana]` that passes when the upstream result is `success` or `skipped` - and make the ruleset require that gate's context instead of the nested "Qodana / Qodana". Alternatively, run Qodana for forks without QODANA_TOKEN in a non-cloud mode, or drop it from the required set and keep it informational as ci.yml already does (ci.yml:132-135 marks the main-branch Qodana job continue-on-error: true). Whichever is chosen, confirm on a real fork PR that all seven required contexts report.

findings.title: Contributor documentation routes public users to GitHub Discussions (disabled) and to label URLs that do not match the repository's actual label names
findings.claim: Marble #566 was closed as `not_planned` and Discussions was never enabled (`has_discussions: false`), but the documentation that #566 was supposed to update was never reverted. CONTRIBUTING.md:87 offers "[Open Discussions](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)" as a starting point and CONTRIBUTING.md:445 makes it the single answer for "**Questions**" - neither can resolve to a discussions page while the feature is off. In the same block, CONTRIBUTING.md:85-86 links `/labels/good-first-issue` and `/labels/help-wanted`, but the repository's 45 labels include "good first issue" and "help wanted" (with spaces) and neither hyphenated slug exists, so both links land on an empty/invalid label filter. Compounding it, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml` does not exist, so the new-issue chooser presents no contact links and offers no alternative route.
findings.failure_scenario: A first-time contributor arriving from the public README opens CONTRIBUTING.md to find something to work on: both 'good first issue' links show nothing, and the 'Questions' route 404s. With no config.yml contact links and Discussions off, the only remaining channel is a public issue - which is also where SECURITY.md tells people NOT to put a suspected vulnerability, so a confused reporter has no visible correct destination short of reading SECURITY.md in full.
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque -> "has_discussions": false; issue #566 state_reason "not_planned"
CONTRIBUTING.md:87 '- [Open Discussions](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)'
CONTRIBUTING.md:445 '- **Questions**: Open a [Discussion](https://github.com/JetBrains-Research/opaque/discussions)'

CONTRIBUTING.md:85-86 link /labels/good-first-issue and /labels/help-wanted; GET /repos/.../labels?per_page=100 returns 45 labels containing 'good first issue' and 'help wanted', and neither 'good-first-issue' nor 'help-wanted'
ls .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ -> bug_report.yml, documentation.yml, feature_request.yml only; no config.yml
findings.fix_sketch: Either enable Discussions (reopening the #566 decision) or remove both Discussions links from CONTRIBUTING.md and point 'Questions' at the issue tracker with a `question` label. URL-encode the real label names in the two 'good starting points' links (`/labels/good%20first%20issue`, `/labels/help%20wanted`). Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml with `blank_issues_enabled` set deliberately and contact_links covering security reporting and questions, so the new-issue chooser routes people correctly.

findings.title: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is disabled on the public repository and SECURITY.md states no concrete disclosure window
findings.claim: SECURITY.md tells reporters to use a private channel and explicitly forbids public issues or discussions for suspected vulnerabilities, but the GitHub-native private path is off: GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/private-vulnerability-reporting returns {"enabled": false}, so the repository's Security tab shows no 'Report a vulnerability' button and an outside researcher's only private route is the security@jetbrains.com mailto at SECURITY.md:12. The policy also never states a disclosure window; SECURITY.md:41-42 only asks reporters to 'allow reasonable time for a fix or mitigation before public disclosure' and delegates the timeline to the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy (SECURITY.md:38-40), which is a real, reachable document but is not the project-specific window Marble #554 framed.
findings.failure_scenario: A researcher who finds a privacy-accounting defect with material impact clicks the repository's Security tab, sees no reporting form (the standard 2026 workflow), and either discloses publicly in an issue - which SECURITY.md:14 forbids and which for a DP library means publishing an under-noising defect before a fix - or abandons the report. Because no window is stated, a reporter who does email has no basis for deciding when publication is fair, and neither side has a shared expectation.
evidence: GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque/private-vulnerability-reporting -> HTTP 200, {"enabled": false}
GitHub API GET /repos/JetBrains-Research/opaque -> "private": false, "visibility": "public"
SECURITY.md:10-14 'Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to security@jetbrains.com ... Do not open a public issue or discussion for a suspected vulnerability.'
SECURITY.md:41-42 'Please allow reasonable time for a fix or mitigation before public disclosure.' — no number of days anywhere in the file
https://www.jetbrains.com/legal/docs/terms/coordinated-disclosure/ -> HTTP 200 (the delegated policy is real and reachable)
findings.fix_sketch: Enable private vulnerability reporting in repository Settings -> Security (one toggle; it also unlocks draft GitHub Security Advisories for the published opaque-* distributions) and mention that route first in SECURITY.md alongside the email. Add a concrete acknowledgement and disclosure expectation - e.g. acknowledge within N business days, coordinate publication within 90 days or on fix release, whichever is first - or state explicitly that the JetBrains Coordinated Disclosure Policy's timeline governs and link the specific clause.

findings.title: Removing the contract tests (#586) left the documented torch-free opaque-accounting guarantee with no automated enforcement, in the repository or post-build
findings.claim: 864a6442 (#587, closing Marble #586) deleted tests/contracts/test_accounting_torch_free.py and tests/contracts/test_accounting_factory_leakage.py along with the fragile enumeration checks. The torch-free test was not a structural proxy - it enforced a guarantee the project advertises as a supported installation option (README.md:44 'torch-free standalone'; docs/getting-started/installation.md; packages/opaque-base/pyproject.toml:26-30 'Adding any third-party dependency here would propagate into opaque-accounting ... and break the "torch-free accounting" guarantee'; AGENTS.md installation matrix 'pip install opaque-accounting  # PLD accounting (torch-free standalone)'). Nothing replaced it: a repo-wide grep finds no remaining test asserting the property, and .github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml runs exactly one scenario - install `opaque[all]` and compose a DP-SGD and a DP-FTRL process - never an opaque-accounting-only install in a torch-free environment. The ARC-004/ARC-005/ARC-011 post-build validation meant to take over is still marked 'Planned' in .junie/architecture-contracts.md.
findings.failure_scenario: A future change adds `import torch` (or a torch-importing helper) to packages/opaque-accounting/src or to its tests. Every CI lane passes, because the test runner's environment always has torch installed via the other workspace packages. The published opaque-accounting wheel then declares only opaque-base as a dependency but fails to import in the torch-free environment the README, AGENTS.md and installation docs promise - discovered only by an end user. I verified the property currently still holds (no torch import anywhere under packages/opaque-accounting/{src,tests}; its only dependency is opaque-base>=0.0.0.dev0), so this is an unguarded invariant, not a live break.
evidence: git show 864a6442 --stat — deletes tests/contracts/test_accounting_torch_free.py (55 lines) and tests/contracts/test_accounting_factory_leakage.py (89 lines), plus 8 other enumeration/import tests
git show 864a6442^:tests/contracts/test_accounting_torch_free.py — AST-scanned packages/opaque-accounting/{src,tests} for `import torch` / `from torch...`
.github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml:50-88 — the single 'Run cross-stack scenario' step installs "${opaque_wheels[0]}[all]" and imports opaque.dpftrl/opaque.dpsgd; no torch-free install path
grep -rn 'torch_free|torch-free' over the tree returns only prose/comments (packages/opaque-base/pyproject.toml:26,30; two module docstrings) and one unrelated auditing test comment — no enforcement
.junie/architecture-contracts.md contract table — ARC-004 Backend-neutral distributions: Planned; ARC-005: Planned; ARC-011 Supported installation options: Planned

Current property verified holding: no `import torch` / `from torch` under packages/opaque-accounting/{src,tests}; packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:13-15 dependencies = ["opaque-base>=0.0.0.dev0"]
findings.fix_sketch: Add one backend-neutral scenario to .github/workflows/validate-distributions.yml: create a venv, install only the built opaque_accounting and opaque_base wheels with --no-deps plus their real deps, assert `torch` is not importable in that venv, and run a minimal accounting operation (e.g. gaussian(1.0) composed and epsilon_at(1e-5)). That is behavioural post-build validation - what ARC-004/ARC-011 describe - so it restores the guard without reintroducing the source-scanning check #586 removed.

findings.title: A 60 KB internal research diary sits at the public repository root, unreferenced by any documentation and carrying stale claims about defects
findings.claim: d09d7b9a (fix(dpftrl): bound BISR noise state by bandwidth (#886), 2026-09-02) committed issue-795-research.md - a 1000+ line, 60 KB 'Research snapshot' working document - to the root of the public repository. It is referenced by nothing: not mkdocs.yml, not README.md, not CONTRIBUTING.md, not docs/. Its content is exactly what AGENTS.md forbids in the tree ('Keep user-facing docs and code comments diary-free: describe the current API and behavior, not the development history ... Migration narrative belongs in PR bodies and the changelog'): rebase provenance, superseded recommendations, and running commentary on other issues. It is also already stale - lines 45-47, 979 and 1014 describe issue #789 as 'the separate, urgent calibrated-resume defect' that 'remains urgent', while #789 was closed as completed on 2026-09-04. Because Marble #558 ('perform a public-facing editorial review') closed on 2026-08-11, this landed three weeks after the editorial gate.
findings.failure_scenario: A prospective user or reviewer browsing the public repository root sees, next to README.md and LICENSE, a document that reads as an internal engineering memo and states that the library has an 'urgent' unfixed privacy-calibration defect. That misrepresents the current state of the project (the defect is fixed), and it is the single most prominent non-README file at the root. Every future reader of the repository root pays that cost, and the document will keep drifting because nothing builds or tests it.

findings.title: AGENTS.md's "Accounting native module" section is factually wrong on all three of its claims and contradicts AGENTS.md's own package table
findings.claim: The "### Accounting native module" block states that the compiled artifact is `opaque/accounting/opaque_accounting.abi3.so`, that maturin is configured with `module-name = "opaque.accounting.opaque_accounting"` and `python-packages = ["opaque.accounting"]`, and that `opaque.accounting/__init__.py` does `from . import opaque_accounting as _native`. None of that is true at 12146ec4. packages/opaque-accounting/pyproject.toml:38-40 sets `module-name = "opaque.api.accounting.core.opaque_accounting"` and `python-packages = ["opaque/accounting", "opaque/api/accounting/core"]`; the built wheel contains exactly one .so at `opaque/api/accounting/core/opaque_accounting.abi3.so`; and the `_native` alias is bound in packages/opaque-accounting/src/opaque/api/accounting/core/__init__.py:16, not in the opaque.accounting facade, whose __init__.py contains no such import. AGENTS.md's own package table earlier in the file already says the extension is at `opaque.api.accounting.core.opaque_accounting`, so the file contradicts itself.
findings.failure_scenario: AGENTS.md is the loaded entry point for every Copilot/Claude agent working in this repository (per .junie/architecture-contracts.md's agent entry-point table). An agent asked to touch the native module follows this section, looks for or edits `opaque/accounting/opaque_accounting`, finds nothing, and either guesses or 'fixes' the maturin configuration back to a layout that does not build - a concrete failure mode given that these three lines are the only place the native layout is documented for agents. AGENTS.md was edited twice in the delta (873de427, ba39783d) without this section being reconciled.
